name: Ishikawa Goemon
contribution: The leader of a group of bandits during the Azuchi-Momoyama period in Japan.

checks.lead: Ishikawa Goemon (石川 五右衛門, Ishikawa Goemon; Japanese pronunciation: [ì.ɕi̥.kä́.β̞ä́ | ɡò̞.é̞.mó̞ɴ́, -β̞ä́ ɡó̞-], August 24, 1558 – October 8, 1594) was the leader of a group of bandits during the Azuchi-Momoyama period in Japan. Over time, and especially during the Edo period (1603–1867), his life and deeds became a center of attention, and he became known as a legendary Japanese outlaw hero who stole gold and other valuables to give to the poor.
